buttonLabel: "Explore wildlife on a route through four countries"
lead: >-
  Chile, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay offer Atacama desert landscapes, the Peruvian Andes and Titicaca, the green surroundings of Guatapé and Montevideo's coast. But on the current eight-country tour, the main wildlife-watching activities lie outside these four countries: on Ecuador's Galápagos Islands, with possible flamingo sightings at Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons. This distinction matters when choosing a journey for birds and wildlife.
---

## Where to watch wildlife on a route through Chile, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay

We have assembled the “Chile, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay: Wildlife and Safaris” selection around the [existing 32-day tour of eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). The journey includes the four selected nations as well as Brazil, Argentina, Bolivia and Ecuador. The theme applies **to the full itinerary**. It does not imply wildlife watching in each of the four highlighted countries.

| Country | Actual focus |
|---|---|
| Chile | Atacama Desert |
| Peru | Andes and Lake Titicaca |
| Colombia | Guatapé and the reservoirs |
| Uruguay | Montevideo and the bay |

**Chile.** After sightseeing in Santiago, travelers head to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). The desert landscape, altitude, remoteness of settlements and preparation for the next Bolivian stage matter here. There is no separate safari, birdwatching activity or guaranteed viewing of particular animal species included during the Chilean days.

**Peru.** The itinerary passes through [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), the [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/), Cusco and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Travelers see Andean scenery and high-altitude lakeshores, but the days are mainly devoted to cultural excursions, transport and historic sites. A natural landscape surrounding Machu Picchu does not equate to an included bird- or wildlife-watching excursion.

**Colombia.** From [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), a trip takes visitors to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/), [El Peñón rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and reservoirs. Scenery is combined with visits to settlements, followed by city excursions in Cartagena and Bogotá. No specialist fauna-watching program is specified for the Colombian days.

**Uruguay.** During a [one-day trip to Montevideo](/uruguay/montevideo/montevideo-day-trip-from-buenos-aires/), travelers explore a coastal city and the Río de la Plata estuary. This excursion focuses on the capital, port and historic center, not marine wildlife or protected natural areas.

## Where wildlife is actually observed on the full journey

The most substantial nature section is in **Ecuador, on the [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/)**. The itinerary includes a flight to the archipelago, a visit to the highlands of [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/) and one of two sea-excursion routes.

The option visiting [North Seymour Island](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/north-seymour-island-tour/) and Bachas beaches focuses on island fauna, including colonies of seabirds such as frigatebirds and blue-footed boobies. The other option visits [South Plaza](/ecuador/galapagos-islands/south-plaza-island-tour/) and Cape Carrión, with an island walk and opportunities to observe sea lions, iguanas and birds. Actual sightings depend on conditions; an animal mentioned in a place description is not a guarantee of an encounter.

**Only one of the two routes is included.** The specific option is confirmed after booking; North Seymour, Bachas, South Plaza and Cape Carrión cannot be combined into one guaranteed excursion day. This is particularly important if you hope to see a particular bird species or island.

Another significant nature experience takes place in Bolivia, at high-altitude lagoons during the two-day jeep route. Flamingos are mentioned around Laguna Colorada in the tour description. Like Ecuador, Bolivia is part of the full eight-country itinerary but is not one of the four countries in this selection's title.

## Choosing a trip when wildlife is your main goal

If photographing animals is your priority, choose **specific excursion days** rather than just a list of countries on the catalog page. For this tour, first confirm whether the Galápagos boat trip can operate, which island option is available, access rules, walking times and restrictions on approaching wildlife.

If varied landscapes are more important, open the [“Nature” selection for these four countries](/multi-country/chile_colombia_peru_uruguay/interests/nature/): from dry Atacama and Peru's highlands to Colombia's green slopes and coastal Uruguay. A substantial share of the trip, however, is devoted to cities, museums and transfers.

The journey lasts 32 days, and wildlife is not the theme of every day. Shortening the itinerary to Chile, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay would **remove the main confirmed wildlife observation opportunities in the Galápagos**. For a tailored version, Ada Tours helps retain the nature stops that matter and coordinate them with flights and local excursions.

## Where to compare other routes

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. For other wildlife-watching options, explore [multi-country “Wildlife and Safaris” journeys](/multi-country/interests/wildlife/) and [wildlife tours featuring Ecuador](/interests/wildlife/tours/ecuador/). The [general Chile, Colombia, Peru and Uruguay catalog](/multi-country/chile_colombia_peru_uruguay/) shows existing routes without filtering by interest.

## Frequently asked questions about wildlife watching

### Will wildlife watching take place in all four selected countries?

That is not confirmed. In Chile, Peru, Colombia and Uruguay, this itinerary mainly features landscape, city and cultural stops. The principal protected-island excursion section with wildlife observation is in Ecuador.

### Can North Seymour and South Plaza be visited in one included day?

No. These are alternative boat routes. The program includes one confirmed option, not both at once.

### What if my goal is to see blue-footed boobies?

Focus on a specific Galápagos excursion, particularly the North Seymour option. Island access and the chance of bird sightings must be checked for your dates; encounters with wild animals cannot be guaranteed.

lead: >-
  With Chile, Colombia and Uruguay, the key question is how much time is spent in each country. On our current 32-day itinerary, Uruguay is a one-day ferry outing from Buenos Aires, Chile includes Santiago and Atacama, and Colombia features several cities at the end of the journey. Substantial stages in other countries separate them, so this is not one continuous three-country trip.
---

## Chile, Colombia and Uruguay: three countries with very different visit durations

When [Uruguay](/uruguay/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Colombia](/colombia/) are selected as filters, it is easy to imagine three stages of equal length. The existing [journey across eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) is arranged differently: Uruguay occupies one excursion day, Chile several days, and Colombia brings the larger itinerary to its conclusion.

This matters for expectations. Someone passionate about Montevideo and Uruguayan culture may find one day insufficient, while a traveler seeking an introduction without an overnight stay may find the format ideal. The selection displays {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}; before choosing, look at each actual route, not just the number of country names in the filter.

## Uruguay: Montevideo and a return to Argentina

The itinerary organizes the day in [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) **as a round trip from Buenos Aires**. In the morning, travelers transfer to the port, take a ferry across the Río de la Plata, tour the city with an English-speaking guide, enjoy free time and return to their hotel in Argentina in the evening. Ferry tickets are listed as included for that day.

The excursion covers [Montevideo's port](/uruguay/place/montevideo-port/), [Independence Square](/uruguay/place/montevideo-independence-square/), the [Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/) and the [cathedral](/uruguay/place/montevideo-cathedral/). No overnight stay in Uruguay is included.

In practice, travelers need to coordinate **at least two sets of border formalities in one day**, arrival at the ferry, return timing and valid documents for re-entry to Argentina. The ferry stage requires extra time before departure and information about baggage allowances. Schedule changes may affect the following day, when the flight to Chile is planned.

## Chile: from city neighborhoods to high-altitude Atacama

After the Argentine stage, the group flies to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). A city tour, including the historic center, is planned. An additional visit to the Maipo Valley wineries is offered separately from the mandatory itinerary.

Next comes a flight to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/) before the high-altitude road into Bolivia. A nighttime astronomy excursion is optional and subject to operating conditions. Unlike Uruguay, the Chilean section includes both city and nature settings and requires more preparation for elevation.

Packing needs particular care: warm clothes for cool desert evenings, sun protection and comfortable shoes. Bringing only clothing for warm South American weather would be a mistake.

## Colombia: a substantial final stage

Travelers reach Colombia much later, after Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/) is the base for a trip to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and a city tour including Comuna 13. The itinerary then takes a flight to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/) for sightseeing in the historic center, followed by a flight to [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/) and a trip to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/).

Colombia receives considerably more time than Uruguay. This allows travelers to experience several different kinds of city but also means extra flight connections and the need to keep track of baggage on each segment. Light clothes suit Cartagena, while high-altitude Bogotá can be cooler in the evenings.

## How the stages of the full program connect

| Segment | How it works |
|---|---|
| Uruguay | Ferry from Argentina and back |
| Chile | Flight, city, Atacama |
| Colombia | Flights between cities |

Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador lie between the Chilean and Colombian stages. This is not merely “a long transfer” between two selected countries, but a substantial tourism program in its own right, including Uyuni, Machu Picchu and the Galápagos.

If Montevideo and Santiago are your priorities and Colombia is optional, compare [routes combining Chile and Uruguay](/multi-country/chile_uruguay/). If Santiago and Colombia's cities matter more, the choice becomes how many days to retain for the Andes and which countries to include between them. Any shorter version needs a new timetable and price agreement.

## Passport, connections and currency

As of the October 16, 2026 check, official sources confirmed short-term visa-free tourist entry to Chile and Colombia for holders of ordinary Russian international passports. **This is not a single regime covering the entire eight-country program.** Uruguay and Argentina need particular attention: the day excursion involves leaving Argentina and subsequently returning. Entry rules, passport validity and documents required for re-entry must be checked for the traveler's nationality and itinerary. Other passport nationalities may require different checks.

The three selected countries have different national currencies: the Uruguayan, Chilean and Colombian pesos. Do not assume US dollars will be accepted on every excursion or in every café. Plan payment methods, a small cash reserve and an understanding of which currency a foreign card charges. Russian-issued cards operating through international networks generally do not work abroad.

Chile checks imports of plants and animal products when entering by air or overland. If you buy food or souvenirs during the Uruguay excursion, check the restrictions on carrying them onward before putting them in your suitcase.

## What to agree before buying

First, do you want **an overnight stay in Uruguay**, or is a day excursion enough? Second, is the high-altitude stage beyond Chile important? Third, how many days would you like in Colombia's cities? These are three different variables, and a standard set of country filters does not answer them all.

The current catalog lets you open the exact route, conditions, duration and price of the full itinerary:

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

We help coordinate country order, citizenship-related documents, ferry and flight connections and sightseeing time. A different duration or extra overnight stays require a fresh check of transport availability and accommodation terms.

## Frequently asked questions about Chile, Colombia and Uruguay

### Does this selection include a tour visiting only the three countries?

The confirmed product is a larger eight-country itinerary. The selection indicates that all three countries are part of its principal geography; it does not automatically create a separate three-country product.

### Is an overnight stay in Montevideo included?

No. On the existing route, Montevideo is a one-day ferry excursion from Buenos Aires, returning to Argentina for the night.

### Why not travel straight from Chile to Colombia?

Because the program includes a substantial stage across Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. A direct flight-based itinerary would require separate planning.

### Is one visa check sufficient?

No. You must account for Uruguay, re-entry to Argentina, Chile, Colombia and every intermediate country on the actual route; requirements depend on citizenship and travel dates.

lead: >-
  Chile, Colombia and Uruguay are part of a longer journey through eight South American countries. The Chilean stage leads from Santiago to Atacama, Colombia introduces Guatapé and Andean cities, and Uruguay is visited on a one-day trip to Montevideo. Here we explain which active experiences are actually included and how to plan the physical demands without false expectations.

## What adventures await in Chile, Colombia and Uruguay?

This selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The main option is a [32-day journey across eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/), which also crosses Brazil, Argentina, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. This page highlights **three countries within the larger itinerary**, not a separate trip restricted to Chile, Colombia and Uruguay.

For active travelers, the differences matter. In [Chile](/chile/), the program combines [Santiago](/chile/) and the high-altitude surroundings of San Pedro de Atacama, preparing travelers for the next stage in Bolivia. [Colombia](/colombia/) includes a trip to El Peñón de Guatapé and city walks. [Uruguay](/uruguay/) is represented by a day in Montevideo, with a ferry and city sightseeing rather than trekking.

| Country | Confirmed experience |
|---|---|
| Chile | Santiago, transfer to Atacama, acclimatization |
| Colombia | El Peñón rock, Guatapé, Medellín |
| Uruguay | Ferry, Montevideo, city tour |

**The itinerary does not promise sporting treks, rafting and ascents in all three countries.** The adventure theme applies to the entire trip. Its most pronounced off-road stage, a two-day 4×4 jeep journey through lagoons and salt flats, takes place in **Bolivia**. It is useful to understand this before selecting a tour: a busy itinerary through contrasting landscapes and many flights calls for different preparation from a specialist trekking holiday.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

## Chile: the transition from city to desert and altitude

The Chilean section begins with a flight from Buenos Aires to Santiago. The following day includes a tour of the capital with a Russian-speaking guide. A flight to Calama and a transfer to San Pedro de Atacama then follow. The itinerary explicitly mentions **acclimatization before Uyuni**: the Chilean stage is followed by overland travel in Bolivia's highlands.

[San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/) is interesting as a starting point for expeditions into desert and mountain scenery. On this particular tour, however, its principal role is transit and adjustment. A nighttime astronomy excursion is available as an optional extra in English, subject to viewing conditions and confirmation. It must not be regarded as included or guaranteed.

Changes in elevation and temperature matter more than the number of city stops. Spring clothing suits Santiago, while the desert calls for a warm evening layer, sun protection, closed comfortable shoes and water. Travelers should also discuss individual altitude-related limitations with a doctor, particularly if they have heart or lung conditions. Spending the previous night in San Pedro does not make the subsequent Bolivian jeep stage any less high-altitude.

Readers seeking genuinely strenuous outdoor activities in Chile should compare [adventure tours featuring Chile](/interests/adventure/tours/chile/) by their actual walking days. The word “Atacama” in a route name does not by itself imply multi-day trekking.

## Colombia: Guatapé and urban walks rather than extreme sports

The Colombian stage comes near the end: arrival in Medellín, a trip to El Peñol and Guatapé, a city tour including Comuna 13, then Cartagena, Bogotá and Zipaquirá.

The excursion to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) includes an introduction to [El Peñón de Guatapé](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/). This is a striking natural landmark above the reservoir, but a sporting ascent, rock-climbing routes and a climb up the steps are distinct activities. Actual access to the lookout and the physical demands must be confirmed against the excursion's terms; the rock's presence in the itinerary does not establish that all these activities are included.

Medellín features a city tour and Comuna 13. Cartagena offers its historic center; Bogotá has museums and Monserrate, followed by a visit to the Zipaquirá Salt Mines. These are busy walking and sightseeing days, but they do not replace a specialist mountain program. After flights, allowing time for sleep and a calm evening is more sensible than filling every available slot with optional activities.

For a broader selection within the country, explore [tours in Colombia](/colombia/tour/). Compare actual days in nature areas, named activities and their physical difficulty rather than relying solely on the general thematic label.

## Uruguay: one day across the Río de la Plata

[Montevideo](/uruguay/) features as a separate day between the Argentine capital and the flight to Chile. Travelers leave Buenos Aires early for the port, cross the bay and Río de la Plata estuary by ferry, explore Montevideo with an English-speaking guide, enjoy free time and return to Buenos Aires.

The adventure here consists of visiting another country and changing transport, not sporting activity. Choosing this itinerary for Uruguayan mountain routes would be a mistake: **the Uruguay stage is urban and lasts one day**. Extra days by the ocean or nature activities beyond the capital would change the itinerary, rather than being existing included excursions.

The ferry requires extra time for boarding and passport control. Schedules must allow for the trip to the port and return to the Argentine hotel. After the Uruguay day, the route leaves Buenos Aires for Santiago, so Argentina cannot be bypassed when planning the full journey.

## How these three countries connect on the actual 32-day journey

The journey **does not follow a direct Chile → Colombia → Uruguay chain**. The sequence is different: Montevideo as a day trip from Buenos Aires, then Santiago and Atacama, followed by Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador, with Colombia at the end. Border and flight requirements therefore cover **all eight principal countries**, not just the three selected ones.

This kind of trip requires allowance for domestic flights, possible baggage problems, changing weather and physical recovery after altitude. The greatest demands come not from the Uruguay day but from the high-altitude stage and packed days with several transfers. We help arrange reasonable connections, choose a suitable sightseeing pace and check which stages can be adapted to the group. Whether the specific itinerary can be changed is confirmed when planning.

Weather also differs: spring conditions in Montevideo and Santiago, the dry highlands of Atacama and Colombia's warmer cities call for layered clothing. An outfit intended for only one climate zone will not work. Keep doctor-prescribed medications, essential spare clothing and documents for consecutive border crossings in your hand luggage.

## Documents, payments and insurance

For Russian citizens, entry requirements must be checked **for each country individually**, including Argentina, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador on the full route. Visa-free entry rights, duration of stay and transit permits cannot be inferred simply because the trip is sold as one itinerary. We help prepare a checklist based on citizenship, passport, dates, tickets and entry sequence; border officials make the admission decision.

The three selected countries use different national currencies: Chilean pesos, Colombian pesos and Uruguayan pesos. Argentine pesos are also needed for the ferry stage and nights in Argentina. Check exchange rates, foreign-card acceptance and options for Russian bank cards for the relevant dates. Holding US dollars in cash does not, by itself, replace local payment arrangements.

For a journey with high-altitude travel and several flights, the insurance contract deserves particular attention: check geographic coverage across every country, exclusions for high altitudes or activities, medical expense limits and assistance procedures. Travelers need to understand which events their policy actually covers.

## Choosing between the grand route and a trip centered on one activity

If you want to explore several cultural and natural regions of South America on one holiday, the [32-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) offers a coherent journey from Rio to Bogotá. If your main goal is 7–10 days of challenging trekking, compare it with [dedicated adventure journeys](/interests/adventure/) by actual exertion and time on the trail.

The complete country combination, without thematic filtering, is in the [Chile, Colombia and Uruguay catalog](/multi-country/chile_colombia_uruguay/). When choosing, ask four questions: how much time is really spent hiking or off-roading, which countries host those activities, what altitude is reached and who organizes the demanding crossings. These answers are far more precise than the generic “Adventure” label.

## Frequently asked questions about adventure in Chile, Colombia and Uruguay

### Does this itinerary include trekking across Atacama?

The confirmed program includes a flight to Calama, a transfer to San Pedro de Atacama and acclimatization. No separate multi-day desert trek is specified. A nighttime astronomy excursion is offered as an extra.

### Can I climb El Peñón de Guatapé?

The itinerary includes an excursion to the El Peñón and Guatapé area. The actual option and conditions for climbing must be agreed separately, taking site access and physical preparation into account.

### Are there outdoor adventure activities in Uruguay?

The confirmed Uruguay day is a ferry trip to Montevideo and a city tour with a return to Argentina. It does not promise sporting activities.

### What makes the full tour adventurous?

The eight-country itinerary features the highland landscapes of Atacama and Bolivia, a two-day 4×4 off-road route on Bolivia's plateau and many contrasting natural regions. Activities take place in different countries, not evenly across Chile, Colombia and Uruguay.

### Are documents for only these three countries enough?

No. The [eight-country journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) also includes Brazil, Argentina, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. Entry, transit and passport-validity requirements must be checked for every actual border crossing.

## Chile, Colombia and Uruguay: three perspectives on South America

This selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. At present it is centered on a [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Chile, Colombia and Uruguay appear in the catalog title, but the itinerary also includes Brazil, Argentina, Bolivia, Peru and Ecuador. This matters when choosing dates: the three countries occur at different stages of the larger route and do not form a separate, continuous three-country tour.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

The cultural interest takes three different forms here. Uruguay provides a brief introduction to historic Montevideo, Chile offers the square and neighborhoods of Santiago, and Colombia offers several days in Medellín, Cartagena and Bogotá. [All routes featuring this combination](/multi-country/chile_colombia_uruguay/) let you compare the available journeys without misrepresenting their duration.

| Country | What's included in the route |
|---|---|
| Uruguay | 1 day in Montevideo |
| Chile | Santiago and Atacama |
| Colombia | Medellín, Cartagena, Bogotá |

## Uruguay: one day in Montevideo, returning to Argentina

On the existing itinerary, [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is scheduled for October 30: an early transfer from Buenos Aires to the ferry, the crossing, sightseeing with an English-speaking guide, free time and a return to Buenos Aires in the evening. Ferry tickets are included in the specified tour. There is no separate overnight stay in Uruguay.

That is why the Uruguay cultural stage is best treated as a concentrated introduction to the capital. [Montevideo's Old Town](/uruguay/place/montevideo-old-town/), historic squares and port heritage reveal a city shaped by Spanish colonial development and Atlantic trade. When planning, the ferry timetable, time for port formalities and the return sailing matter, especially with an international flight scheduled for the following day.

A more thorough exploration of Uruguay, its museums and coast would require a separate change to the route. This day should not be advertised as an extensive tour of the country.

## Chile: Santiago's civic history and the transition to the desert

After Buenos Aires, travelers fly to [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). A group city tour with a Russian-speaking guide introduces the central districts. [La Moneda Palace](/chile/place/la-moneda-palace/) provides an opportunity to discuss the country's republican history, while [Plaza de Armas](/chile/place/santiago-plaza-de-armas/) reveals the origins of its colonial center. Buildings around the main square and Santa Lucía Hill offer different views of the capital's development.

The following day brings a change of setting: a flight from Santiago to Calama and a transfer to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). Time to acclimatize is scheduled before the high-altitude stage in Bolivia. The nighttime astronomy excursion is **optional**, so it cannot be counted as part of the mandatory cultural program.

These two Chilean days connect urban history with the transition to Andean landscapes. Anyone mainly interested in Santiago's museums will need more free time for a deeper visit.

## Colombia: from Medellín's transformation to colonial Cartagena

The Colombian stage comes at the end of the longer journey, after Peru and the Galápagos Islands. In [Medellín](/colombia/place/medellin/), a city tour includes [Comuna 13](/colombia/place/comuna-13/). Its street art and public spaces invite discussion of changes to the urban environment. The district's particular stories are best learned with a local guide, without romanticizing a difficult past.

A day is devoted to [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/) and El Peñón rock. This combines nature and small-town architecture rather than being a museum itinerary. The group then flies to [Cartagena](/colombia/place/cartagena/): its historic center, colorful facades and San Felipe de Barajas Castle reveal the Caribbean history of trade, defense and a colonial city.

In [Bogotá](/colombia/place/bogota/), the itinerary explores the historic La Candelaria district, the Gold Museum and [Monserrate](/colombia/place/monserrate-bogota/). The following day features a trip to [Zipaquirá](/colombia/place/zipaquira/) and the Salt Cathedral. Museums have specific closed days: the existing tour explicitly mentions restrictions on Mondays and Tuesdays. Exact visit times are confirmed during planning.

## How these countries connect in the actual itinerary

The journey follows Brazil → Argentina, with a side trip to Uruguay → Chile → Bolivia → Peru → Ecuador → Colombia. It does not feature a direct Santiago–Medellín flight or a sightseeing bus from Montevideo to Colombia. Thus this cultural selection highlights the **main countries of a much longer tour**, not a shortened route with just three stops.

Travel across different periods and regions benefits from a sensible balance of sightseeing days and transfers. Connections after the ferry, flights across several countries and extra time before lengthy excursions are especially important. We coordinate city order, ground transfers and guides within the chosen itinerary; changing its duration or geography requires a separate recalculation of included services.

## Documents, money and weather: what to check in advance

For travelers with an ordinary Russian international passport, official lists as checked on **October 16, 2026** provide for short-term visa-free tourist entry to Colombia and Uruguay. These are two independent entry regimes; Chile's entry conditions, permitted stay and documentation need to be checked against current Chilean immigration and consular rules. Visa-free status does not eliminate the need to check return tickets, accommodation, passport validity and transit requirements along all eight countries. Other nationalities require their own checks.

Three local currencies are used: Chilean pesos, Uruguayan pesos and Colombian pesos. US-dollar transactions may occur in tourism, but day-to-day expenses are easier to plan in local currency. Confirm acceptance of any particular bank card, including those issued in Russia, with its issuer and payment network, and arrange a backup payment method.

It is spring in Montevideo and Santiago in late October and November. Santiago can have cool evenings, and Atacama has noticeable day–night temperature swings. Conditions differ in Colombia: high-altitude Bogotá feels cooler than humid, hot Cartagena, with Medellín between those extremes. A light jacket, comfortable old-town walking shoes and clothing for the warm coast belong in your bag. Check baggage rules for each individual flight.

## Who will enjoy this cultural journey?

This selection suits travelers seeking several South American historical traditions and comfortable with a busy itinerary and frequent transfers. Uruguay offers one day in its capital, Chile covers Santiago and the approach to Atacama, and Colombia has a substantial final stage. If you want a week focused only on these three countries' cities, request a redesigned itinerary rather than treating the 32-day tour as a ready-made three-country version.

You can also compare options in the [multi-country history and culture selection](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/) and [culture-focused tours in Colombia](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/colombia/).

## Frequently asked questions about the culture of Chile, Colombia and Uruguay

### Can I visit these three without the other five countries?

The current catalog features a larger eight-country tour. A shorter itinerary limited to Chile, Uruguay and Colombia would need separately planned flights, overnight stays and pricing.

### How much time is spent in Uruguay?

## Nature in Chile, Colombia and Uruguay: Atacama, Guatapé and the urban shore of the Río de la Plata

In this selection, the three countries feature within a [larger South American tour](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). Their contributions to the natural experience are unequal. In Chile, travelers reach the desert region of [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/); in Colombia, they head to the granite [El Peñón rock](/colombia/place/el-penon-de-guatape/) and lakeside scenery of [Guatapé](/colombia/place/guatape/); and in Uruguay they explore [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) in one day.

**There is no separate nature expedition in Uruguay on the itinerary.** Chile's Patagonian national parks and Colombia's Amazon reserves are also not included. If long walks in natural areas are your main aim, these exclusions matter more than the number of countries in the title.

## Chile: a desert landscape before crossing the border

The Chilean stage begins with a flight to Santiago and a city sightseeing tour. A flight to Calama and a transfer to San Pedro de Atacama follow. Travelers encounter dry Andean landscapes here and prepare for the next high-altitude stage.

An evening telescope-based astronomy excursion is **available at extra cost**. The mandatory itinerary does not include several days exploring all of Atacama's valleys, glacier walks or a trip to Torres del Paine. The colorful lagoons and geothermal fields seen later belong to the Bolivian 4×4 stage.

That leads to a practical choice: if you want volcanic scenery on the way into Bolivia, a short San Pedro stop makes sense. If you would prefer several full days in Chile's natural regions, compare [Chile tours in the “Nature” category](/interests/nature/tours/chile/) and examine their actual excursion days.

## Colombia: water, rock and mountain scenery near Medellín

The clearest nature-oriented day in Colombia is an eight-hour excursion from Medellín to El Peñol, El Peñón rock and Guatapé. A large rock formation, hills, islands and winding reservoir shores lie close together. It offers a chance to see one of central Colombia's recognizable panoramas without arranging a separate multi-day expedition.

The remaining days are devoted to cities: Medellín and Comuna 13, Cartagena, Bogotá, plus a trip to Zipaquirá. These excursions have their own value, but **wildlife observation, jungle trekking and an Amazon safari** are not included as part of the Colombian stage.

Do not automatically treat climbing the steps to the rock's summit as a separately included service: visiting arrangements and physical requirements must be read in the precise day description. Simply visiting Guatapé does not make the entire Colombian section a sporting tour.

## Uruguay: a capital-city excursion, not a national park

Before Chile and Colombia, travelers spend one day in Uruguay. Early in the morning they leave Buenos Aires for the port, cross by ferry to Montevideo and explore the city with an English-speaking guide. They return to Argentina that evening. Ferry tickets are included.

Nature here is chiefly present through the city's coastal location and views over the Río de la Plata. The program focuses on the city, historic buildings and walks. It does not add Uruguayan nature reserves, a multi-day beach holiday or specialist marine excursions.

This is a sensible stop on a larger culture-and-nature journey, but anyone specifically interested in Uruguay's natural attractions needs a different set of places and allocation of days.

## How the transfers are distributed and why these are not three consecutive countries

Uruguay is a one-day side trip from Argentina, returning the same day. The Chilean stage follows, then an extended crossing through Bolivia and Peru, Ecuador with the Galápagos, and only then Colombia. Therefore the three countries on this page **do not form one direct section of the route**.

For travelers, this entails different demands. The Montevideo ferry requires an early departure and careful timing of the return sailing. In Chile, the flight is followed by altitude changes and onward jeep travel in Bolivia. Colombian cities are linked by domestic flights, while the Guatapé nature day requires a lengthy road excursion.

When preparing visas and entry documents for a Russian international passport, account for more than Chile, Colombia and Uruguay: **re-entry to Argentina after the ferry**, as well as all other countries on the full route, also matters. Each country sets its own rules of stay.

## What to pack and how to budget

Weather near San Pedro differs sharply from Colombia's humid regions, while Montevideo in the Southern Hemisphere spring may call for wind protection. In the dry highlands, warm evening clothing, sun protection and water matter; for city walks and Guatapé, pack comfortable footwear and clothes that can be layered for different temperatures.

The currencies differ too: Chilean pesos, Colombian pesos and Uruguayan pesos. Five more countries in the complete journey have other payment arrangements. Determine actual payment and exchange options before flying, taking into account your bank and citizenship; a tour price quoted in dollars says nothing about whether your card works abroad.

## Frequently asked questions about nature in Chile, Colombia and Uruguay

### Is Chilean Patagonia included?

No. The Chilean stops on the existing itinerary focus on Santiago, Calama and San Pedro de Atacama. Patagonia would require a different route.

### Are nature excursions included in Uruguay?

The confirmed Uruguay visit is a city excursion to Montevideo. No specialist nature excursion in Uruguay is included.

### What is the main nature experience in Colombia?

The trip to El Peñón rock and Guatapé. The other Colombian days are predominantly urban and cultural-historical.
